capitals.note: Tasciovanus 'was the first king to mint coins at Verlamion, beginning ca 20 BC'; Ptolemy places the tribe at 'the town of Verlamion (modern St Albans)'. ledger.note: c. 20 BC: coinage at Verlamion. Tasciovanus 'was the first king to mint coins at Verlamion, beginning ca 20 BC' (rulers list: c. 20 BC to AD 9). The date is the start of the coinage, not of a state; the page names Cassivellaunus c. 54 BC only as 'possibly' associated with the tribe.

region.text: Essex around Camulodunum (Colchester), a guess at the extent of the Camulodunum holding; the page gives none

ledger.note: Camulodunum, page silent on date and holder. Tasciovanus's coins were minted there 'ca 15-10 BC' but that advance was given up, and Camulodunum 'was retaken, either by Tasciovanus or by his son Cunobelinus'. The page does not say when; 9 is the year Cunobelinus 'succeeded him ca AD 9 and ruled for about 30 years'. The Trinovantes as the loser is the page's reference to Tasciovanus's expansion; the page does not describe any Trinovantian territory taken by Cunobelinus.

ledger.note: AD 43: Claudius's invasion. The Catuvellauni 'prompted Claudius to launch a successful invasion, led by Aulus Plautius, in AD 43'; Togodumnus (AD 40-43) 'died shortly after the battle on the Thames'; 'The territories of the Catuvellauni became the nucleus of the new Roman province.' The page does not date the annexation of each part separately. Caratacus (rulers list AD 43 to c. 50) was defeated by Ostorius 'in AD 51' and fled to the Brigantes. [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: region set to the whole 9-43 keyframe shape, Essex included; it was the 20 BC-AD 8 shape without Essex.]

sources.title: Catuvellauni
sources.note: Territory, Tasciovanus's coinage at Verlamion from c. 20 BC, Cunobelinus from c. AD 9, Togodumnus and Caratacus, the invasion of AD 43.

notes: A client-free kingdom Cliopatria lacks, the main target of the Claudian invasion. One page opened for this dossier (Catuvellauni); the roman-empire gain of 43 is recorded there with counterpart 'nobody', so this dossier's dissolve names roman-empire without a matching Roman gain. The page gives no area and no frontier; the Camulodunum gain is a conf-1 bridge with the date and the holder both unsettled between Tasciovanus and Cunobelinus. The Trinovantes (Essex), the counterpart named in the gain, are the trinovantes dossier, which ends at 9 with the matching dissolve. Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: Verlamion, Wheathampstead, Camulodunum are not place names (St Albans and Colchester are).
